misreadings.quote: remembering the cheese he once found "inedible"
misreadings.evidence: "some cheese that Gregor had declared inedible two days before"; "In order to test his taste, she brought him a whole selection of things"
misreadings.explanation: The text says Gregor had declared the cheese inedible, but never says Grete remembered this or chose the cheese because of it. The reflection presents her memory and intent as fact, and she is described as simply testing his taste.

misreadings.quote: He sucks greedily at the rotten cheese
misreadings.evidence: "some cheese that Gregor had declared inedible two days before"; "old, half-rotten vegetables"
misreadings.explanation: Only the vegetables are called half-rotten, and the cheese is described only as something Gregor had declared inedible.

misreadings.evidence: "a dish filled with sweetened milk with little pieces of white bread floating in it"
misreadings.explanation: The milk is never called fresh. "Fresh" appears in the text only for the foods Gregor disliked on the newspaper.

misreadings.quote: Gregor spent the night under the couch, finding it the only place where he felt at ease
misreadings.evidence: "he nonetheless felt immediately at ease and his only regret was that his body was too broad to get it all underneath"
misreadings.explanation: The text says he felt at ease under the couch, not that it was the only place where he could.

result.note: The reflection is mostly interpretive and tracks the text; the main fault is attributing to Grete a remembered, deliberate use of the cheese detail, plus a few small embellishments.
